question: Doctors believed 71% of breast cancer patients ranked keeping their breast as a top priority. What share of patients did?
answer: About 7%. Doctors read their patients' wishes through their own assumptions and got this most personal priority wrong tenfold. Mulley, Trimble and Elwyn call it preference misdiagnosis: unlike a wrong diagnosis of disease, it leaves no trace in any record. The patient receives the right treatment for someone else.
move: Never assume what someone wants; ask them, then listen.
ask: Whose wishes am I sure I know, at home or at work, without ever having asked them?
trap: About 70%, close to the doctors' figure, since doctors know patients.
reference: Mulley, Trimble & Elwyn, Patients' preferences matter: stop the silent misdiagnosis, The King's Fund, 2012
